description.p: Roon ships desktop clients for Windows and macOS, but Linux users only get the headless Roon Server and Roon Bridge. Attacca is the daily-driver client Linux never got: browse your library and TIDAL/Qobuz, control every zone, and play to the machine it runs on.

ul.li: Control transport, zones, grouping and volume
Browse your library plus TIDAL and Qobuz, with search and artwork
Show the live play queue and jump to any track in it
Toggle shuffle, repeat and Roon Radio
Respond to media keys and desktop widgets over MPRIS2

description.p: It is built on Roon's official extension API, which sets some limits: the queue cannot be edited beyond jumping within it, and playlist editing, DSP configuration and signal path are not reachable.
A Roon subscription and a Roon Core on your network are required. To play audio on this machine, Roon Bridge must be installed separately — Roon's terms do not permit bundling it.
First alpha: now playing, browse and search, live queue, zone grouping, playback modes and an MPRIS2 bridge.
